title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, Revenue Recognition and Billing Policy (2026)
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood Inference's consolidated Finance & Legal policies for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, procurement and purchase controls, standard contract lifecycle and legal review process, and revenue recognition and billing controls. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, and business owners who create spend or contractual commitments. The policy aligns with our accounting policies, audit controls, and operational processes so that commitments are approved, economically justified, and properly recorded in our systems.

Scope:
- Applies to all global Redwood entities and business units unless a local statutory requirement overrides specific sections below.
- Covers: annual budgeting cycle, monthly/quarterly rolling forecasts, procurement requests and purchase approvals, contract intake and signature, revenue recognition rules for subscription and usage-based offerings, invoicing, collections, and documentation retention.

Objectives:
1. Ensure budgets and forecasts reflect realistic operating plans and provide management with timely visibility into spend and revenue trends.
2. Maintain consistent procurement controls to mitigate financial and compliance risk.
3. Standardize contract intake, legal review, and signature to protect Redwood's risk profile and enable rapid sales/partnership execution.
4. Apply revenue recognition and billing policies that comply with GAAP/ASC 606 and internal revrec standards.

Owners and Responsibilities:
- Finance (FP&A): owner of budgeting and forecasting process, consolidation, variance analysis, and month-end reporting.
- Legal: owner of contract templates, legal review policies, risk approvals, and escalation for non-standard terms.
- Procurement: owner of purchase request workflows, vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and vendor master maintenance.
- Revenue Operations / Billing: owner of invoicing, billing reconciliations, and revenue recognition calculations.
- Business Unit Leaders: accountable for budget accuracy, forecast updates, and approvals for contractual commitments.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting Process
Overview:
- Annual budget prepared by FP&A with inputs from Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, SRE, and GTM. The budget is a zero-based operating plan for the coming fiscal year and includes headcount, cloud/GPU costs, third-party services, and capitalized investments.
- Rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly to reflect actuals and latest assumptions. Quarterly reforecasts at the end of each fiscal quarter.

Key Dates and Deliverables (example FY2026):
1. Budget kickoff: 2025-09-15 (planning assumptions distributed)
2. BU submissions due: 2025-10-30
3. Consolidation and review: 2025-11-01 to 2025-11-21
4. Leadership budget review & approval: 2025-12-01 to 2025-12-15
5. Board submission: 2026-01-10

Budgeting Controls:
- All headcount must be accompanied by a hiring plan and costed to role grade and location.
- Capital projects (>= $50k) require a capital request form, ROI analysis, and Director+ approval.
- Any new subscription or SaaS commitment > $25k annual must include options analysis and Procurement sign-off.

Forecasting Rules:
- Forecasts must be supported by drivers (e.g., ARR by cohort, average deal size, consumption curves).
- Sales and Revenue Ops must provide a committed/closed forecast and an upside/opportunity layer separated for transparency.
- Variance explanations for month-over-month changes > 5% in major line items are required in the monthly FP&A pack.

2) Procurement and Purchase Controls
Procurement Workflow (high-level):
1. Requestor opens a Purchase Requisition (PR) in the procurement system with business justification and budget code.
2. Direct manager approves the PR confirming budget availability.
3. Procurement owns vendor selection, negotiation of standard terms, and issuance of PO.
4. Legal is looped for contract reviews per the thresholds below.
5. Accounts Payable processes invoices against matched POs and receipts.

Approval Matrix (thresholds):
- <$5,000: Manager approval; Procurement optional.
- $5,000 - $25,000: Director approval + Procurement review.
- $25,000 - $100,000: VP approval + Procurement & Legal notification.
- >$100,000: Finance Director + Legal approval + Executive sponsor (SVP/CEO)

Vendor Onboarding Requirements:
- Standard vendor questionnaire (security posture, data handling, sanctions screening) must be completed for any vendor with access to customer data or hosting services.
- Procurement must obtain W-9/Company registration and bank details prior to PO issuance.

Procurement Exceptions:
- Emergency purchases (e.g., incident mitigation) can be approved retroactively by Finance and Procurement; requester must document rationale within 5 business days.

3) Contracts and Legal Process
Contract Intake and Standard Templates:
- Use standard contract templates maintained in the Legal template library: Master Services Agreement (MSA), Data Processing Addendum (DPA), Statement of Work (SOW), Reseller Agreement, Subprocessor Addendum.
- Non-standard clauses must be marked and justified in the contract intake form.

Contract Review Thresholds:
- Standard MSA (no redlines): Legal review not required for renewals < 12 months and <$25k ARR if using approved playbooks.
- Any terms that change liability, indemnity, data residency, or billing models require Legal review.
- Exceptions to standard intellectual property clauses, or customer-suggested audit rights, require Counsel approval.

Signature Authority:
- Sales AE / Manager: can request MSA/SOW but cannot sign on behalf of the company.
- Finance Director: authorized to sign contracts up to $250k ARR with Legal concurrence.
- General Counsel or CEO: required for contracts > $250k ARR or any contract with unusual legal exposure.

Contract Lifecycle Checklist:
1. Intake form completed in CLM (contract lifecycle management) system.
2. Legal assigns template or negotiates changes.
3. Risk approvals obtained if non-standard terms present.
4. Final countersigned copy uploaded to CLM and linked to CRM (SFDC).
5. PO or billing schedule created and routed to RevOps.

4) Revenue Recognition (RevRec) and Billing Policy
Principles:
- Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate transaction price, recognize revenue as obligations are satisfied.

Commercial Models and RevRec Treatment:
1. Hosted API (usage-based): Revenue recognized as usage is invoiced/consumed. For monthly billing, revenue is recorded in the month usage occurred or, when billed in arrears, recognized when performance obligation satisfied and collectibility is probable.
2. Dedicated/Reserved capacity (subscriptions): Typically recognized ratably over the contractual term unless a distinct performance obligation indicates a different pattern. Upfront payments are deferred and recognized monthly.
3. Professional services (implementation): Recognize based on milestone completion if milestone represents a separate performance obligation; otherwise, recognize over time using input method if services are integral to the hosted offering.
4. Multi-element arrangements: Allocate transaction price to performance obligations using relative standalone selling prices or best estimates when not directly observable.

Billing and Invoicing:
- Standard terms: Net 30 unless customer contract specifies otherwise.
- Invoice creation: RevOps generates invoices from the billing system; invoices must reference the contract/SOW/PO and include line-item detail of fees, discounts, and taxes.
- Credit memos and adjustments: require approvals from Revenue Manager and Finance Director for credits > $5,000.

Collections and Bad Debt:
- Collections workflow: automatic reminders at 15, 30, 60, 90 days followed by escalation to Customer Success and Sales.
- Write-offs: any receivable to be written off requires CFO approval and supporting documentation.

Revenue Controls and Audit Evidence:
- All recognized revenue must be traceable to contract documents stored in CLM and supporting billing records in the billing system.
- Monthly revrec reconciliations performed by Revenue Operations and reviewed by Finance (variance thresholds: investigatory threshold = 0.5% of monthly revenue or $25k, whichever is greater).

5) Internal Controls, Segregation of Duties and Documentation Retention
- Segregation of duties: Requestors and approvers of spend cannot be the owner of AP vendor payments for the same vendor. Contract negotiators must not be primary invoice approvers for the same counterparty.
- Documentation retention: Contracts and procurement documents retained for a minimum of 7 years. Finance records retained according to the Records Retention Schedule.
- Audit readiness: maintain an auditable trail in CLM, procurement system, ERP, and S3 evidence buckets.

6) Escalation and Exceptions
- Non-standard legal terms, large commercial concessions, or contract disputes escalate to Legal Counsel and the Finance Director.
- Procurement exceptions requests (e.g., sole-source vendors) must include business justification, risk acceptance, and be approved by Procurement Director and Finance.

KPIs and Reporting:
- Budget variance (monthly) by cost center and by major expense category.
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) target: 45 days.
- Percent of contracts executed within SLA (target: 95% within 10 business days).
- Forecast accuracy: variance vs actuals <= 5% for top-line on a rolling 12-month basis.

Appendices
A. Sample Purchase Requisition Fields:
- Requestor name, cost center, business justification, vendor name, estimated annual spend, GL account, required delivery date.

B. Contract Intake Checklist:
- Customer name, contract type, start/end dates, auto-renewal terms, termination rights, indemnity/limitation of liability changes, data transfer/subprocessor exposure, pricing and billing schedule, signature authority.

C. RevRec Examples (illustrative):
- $120k annual reserved capacity contract paid upfront on 1-Jan-2026: defer $120k and recognize $10k per month over 12 months.
- Usage invoice of $45k billed on 15-Feb-2026 for January usage: recognize $45k in January (performance obligation satisfied in January) and record receivable upon invoicing if collectibility is probable.

D. Helpful Links:
